## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukhavihārijātaka* (Ja 10) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. According to its traditional introductory narrative (*nidāna*), the Buddha recounted the story while residing at the Anupiya Mango-grove near Anupiya, occasioned by the Elder Bhaddiya (the Happy). Bhaddiya had renounced worldly life alongside five other Sakyan nobles and the barber Upāli; among them, Bhaddiya, Kimbila, Bhagu, and Upāli subsequently attained arahantship, Ānanda attained stream-entry, Anuruddha gained the divine eye, and Devadatta achieved supernormal powers. The text opens with the thematic verse reflection beginning “The man who guards not,” and refers the detailed background of the six nobles leading to Anupiya to the *Khaṇḍahāla-jātaka*.
